When a Matrix Is Factorized Sparsely

Source: R/inference.R
worth_sparse.Rd

Returns whether a symmetric matrix is large enough and sparse enough that a sparse Cholesky factorization is used in place of a dense one. The decision depends only on the matrix, and not on any term, any model or any preference of the caller.

Usage

worth_sparse(M, min_dim = 100L, max_density = 0.1)

Arguments

M

A symmetric matrix.

min_dim

The smallest order for which a sparse factorization is used.

max_density

The largest fraction of nonzero entries for which a sparse factorization is used.

Value

A single logical.

Details

A matrix is factorized sparsely when it is stored as an S4 sparse matrix, its order is at least min_dim and its fraction of nonzero entries is at most max_density. Below about a hundred coefficients the sparse route is slower, because its fixed cost is the coercion and the S4 dispatch around it, which does not shrink with the matrix. The size condition prevents this on the fully dense penalized information of a single smooth.

Both quantities are read from the matrix, and the first is its storage. A matrix held as a base matrix is never factorized sparsely, whatever its zeros. This is not a test of the term that produced the matrix. statmod_information_at() accumulates into the design's own kind, so the penalized matrix is stored sparsely exactly when the design is. modelterms7 settles the storage of a block at build when sparse = NULL, the default, and builds it sparse where the product of the number of rows and the number of indicator columns exceeds \(10^5\); sparse = TRUE and sparse = FALSE force the sparse and the dense storage. Where the storage is dense the factorization is a small share of the time of a fit, which is spent in the \(O(np^2)\) products against the design, and coercing a dense \(p \times p\) matrix here to save a share of that size would cost more than it returns.
